analyses.what_happens: Reset ends at edge 1. At edge 4 a PutPartialData (opcode 1, a_size=2, mask 1111) to 0x000 with data 0x6f6200a2 is accepted (acc_w=1). Its bit 0 is 0 and bit 31 is 0, so it is not a qualifying write, and in the RTL it clears ALERT_TEST.regwen. Its D beat is at edge 5 with o_d_error=0. At edge 6 a PutPartialData with a_size=0 and mask 1111 to 0x000 is accepted. That is a malformed request: its response at edges 7-9 has o_d_error=1, and tlul_adapter_reg.sv:158 blocks the register write. Because that response is held back (i_d_ready=0 at edges 7 and 8), o_a_ready=0 at edges 7-9. At edges 8 and 9 the host presents a new request with i_a_valid=1 and i_a_intg_flip=1 (opcode 0, addr 0xC6, source 0). It is never accepted: o_a_ready=0 at edges 8 and 9, and rst_ni falls at edge 10. o_alert=1 at edge 9. At that edge flip_now_w=0, because flip_seen and the checker's flip term are both set only on acc_w. There is also no qualifying write, so q_cnt=0, qual_w=0, a_cnt=0 and age=31. Both clauses of a_CHK_003 fail at edge 9 (nnc_chk_alert.sv:112-115).
analyses.spec_says: rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:604-606 (INT-INTG-002): "When i_a_intg_flip is 1, bit 0 of a_user.cmd_intg is inverted. The request then has a command integrity error: a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault ..., which triggers the fatal_fault alert (section 5)." This does not say the request must first be accepted. D-010, line 668 (RT-8-16): "o_alert shall pulse no later than 16 cycles after the request with i_a_intg_flip = 1 is accepted". That is an upper bound measured from acceptance. It does not forbid an earlier alert. D-009, line 667 (RT-8-14) bounds alert pulses caused by ALERT_TEST writes "with no other alert cause". The contract (contract.json:302) is what moves the start of the exemption to acceptance: "flip_seen: set at the acceptance edge of any request with i_a_intg_flip=1". D-014, line 672, lets the bench issue requests without assuming o_a_ready=1, so presenting a request while a_ready=0 is legal.
analyses.rtl_does: In the wrapper, ot_rv_timer_nnc.sv:78-81 inverts cmd_intg[0] whenever i_a_intg_flip=1, whether or not the request is accepted. tlul_cmd_intg_chk.sv:44 computes `err_o = tl_i.a_valid & (|err | (|data_err))`, so the error is gated by a_valid only, not by a_ready. This is upstream OpenTitan code. rv_timer_reg_top.sv:58-61 and 87 then give `intg_err_o = err_q | intg_err | reg_we_err`, with err_q latching it permanently (lines 77-83). rv_timer.sv:144 and 162 drive this into alert_req_i of prim_alert_sender, and the receiver reports it on o_alert. The pulse therefore comes from the bad-integrity request that was presented at edge 8 and never accepted. It cannot come from an ALERT_TEST write: the edge-4 write had data[0]=0 and cleared regwen (rv_timer_reg_top.sv:175, 615-619), and the edge-6 write was blocked by err_internal (tlul_adapter_reg.sv:158, 281).
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_alert.sv:66 defines `flip_now_w = flip_seen || (acc_w && i_a_intg_flip)`, and line 81 sets flip_seen only `if (acc_w && i_a_intg_flip)`. A flip request that is presented (i_a_valid=1) but not yet accepted, or never accepted, does not stop the check. Lines 112-115 then require q_cnt+qual_w-qerr >= a_cnt+1 and a recent qualifying write for every o_alert pulse.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec (INT-INTG-002, lines 604-606) says a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 triggers the alert. D-010 (line 668) gives only an upper bound from acceptance and does not forbid an earlier alert. The RTL raises the integrity error as soon as a_valid=1 (tlul_cmd_intg_chk.sv:44), so a fatal alert cause is present from the first edge the flip request is presented. The checker exempts only from acceptance (nnc_chk_alert.sv:66, 81), so it counts a legitimately caused fatal alert as spurious.
candidates.evidence_against: The contract text (contract.json:302) explicitly says flip_seen is set at acceptance, so the checker matches its contract. If the contract itself is wrong, the change belongs to the contract as well as the checker.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec never says whether a command-integrity fault on a request that is presented but not accepted (or is withdrawn by reset) counts as a fault. D-010 measures only from acceptance. The contract chose the acceptance edge, and that choice is the point of disagreement.
candidates.evidence_against: INT-INTG-002 ties the alert to "the request" carrying bad integrity, with no acceptance condition. The 16-cycle bound in D-010 is only an upper limit, so a reading that allows an earlier alert fits all of the text.

candidates.evidence_for: Under the contract's reading, an alert before the flip request is accepted counts as spurious.
candidates.evidence_against: No spec sentence requires the integrity check to be gated by a_ready. The behaviour is unmodified OpenTitan tlul_cmd_intg_chk (a_valid gating). A fatal fault on a malformed request on the bus is the intended security response.

candidates.evidence_for: The flip request is dropped by reset without being accepted. ENV-02 (nnc_env.sv:116-128) is guarded by rst_ni, so this is allowed.
candidates.evidence_against: The alert at edge 9 comes before rst_ni falls, while the request is still validly held (i_a_valid=1, o_a_ready=0), so holding it longer would not remove the failure. D-014 (line 672) allows requests while a_ready=0, and D-016 allows reset at any time. No spec rule forbids presenting a flip request while a response is pending.

analyses.options: B (recommended): in nnc_chk_alert.sv, set flip_seen and flip_now_w at any edge with rst_ni=1, i_a_valid=1 and i_a_intg_flip=1, not only on acc_w, and update the contract text of CHK-003 (contract.json:302) to match. Review the same acceptance-based disable in the other checks: nnc_chk_intr.sv:59 `dis = seen_flip || (acc && i_a_intg_flip)`, and the flip disables of CHK-005, CHK-009, CHK-010 and CHK-012. C: if the designer wants the alert tied strictly to acceptance, record that as a new D-xxx decision in section 8. The RTL would then have to be judged against it (A), and this would mean changing upstream tlul_cmd_intg_chk semantics. Do not add an environment assumption that forbids flip requests while a_ready=0: the spec does not support it.

analyses.what_happens: Reset ends at edge 1. At edge 2 a PutFullData (opcode 0) with a_size=1, mask 0011 and data 0x40000001 to 0x100 (INTR_ENABLE0) is accepted. It is a legal, aligned half-word write. Its D beat is at edge 3 with o_d_error=0 (dw0=1, c100 goes back to 0). In the RTL this sets IE_0=1. At edge 3 a PutFullData with a_size=0 and mask 0001 to 0x108 (INTR_TEST0), data 1, is presented. It is accepted at edge 4 and sets IS_0=1. Its response is held at edges 5 and 6 (i_d_ready=0). At edge 6 o_intr_timer_expired=1. The checker's ie is still 0, because the half-word write was not a modelled ie update. At edge 6: c100=0, dw0/dw1/dw2=0 (the D beat of the 0x100 write was at edge 3, outside edges k-2..k = 4..6), and there was no flip. So a_CHK_004 fires at edge 6.
analyses.spec_says: D-005, rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:663 (RT-8-07): "o_intr_timer_expired shall equal IS_0 AND IE_0 except in the 2 cycles after either changes." The comportability rule CP-T1.8.6-04 says the same: "The output of the INTR_STATE register becomes the outgoing interrupt to the processor after masking (ANDing) with the value of INTR_ENABLE." IE_0 is the rw field at bit 0, and bits 31:1 are reserved (RT-T5.4.1-01). Register tool, opentitan_register_tool.md:689-695: errors only for "writes of size smaller than register size" ("The width of the register is determined by the location of its fields") and for sub-32b writes that are not word-aligned. INTR_ENABLE0 has width 1, so an aligned 16-bit write is legal and takes effect. D-013 (line 671): "Non-contiguous masks and other sub-word cases are not checked". This says they are not checked; it does not say they are excluded. INT-TL-003 (lines 594-595) makes such requests legal stimulus.
analyses.rtl_does: rv_timer_reg_pkg.sv:150 gives `4'b 0001` as the PERMIT for INTR_ENABLE0. In rv_timer_reg_top.sv:601-611, wr_err = reg_we & (PERMIT & ~reg_be), which is 0 for be=0011. tlul_err.sv:70-74 accepts a_size=1 at addr[1:0]=0 with mask 0011 (fulldata_chk = &mask[1:0]). rv_timer_reg_top.sv:623-625 sets `intr_enable0_we = ... & reg_we & !reg_error` and `intr_enable0_wd = reg_wdata[0]`, so IE_0 becomes 1. The INTR_TEST0 byte write (lines 629-631) then sets IS_0, and the interrupt output is IS_0&IE_0. This matches D-005 and CP-T1.8.6-04.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_intr.sv:68-70 updates ie only for writes to 0x100 with (a_size=2, mask 1111) or (a_size=0, mask 0001). The update happens at the D beat with d_error=0 (line 104). Line 61 tracks any write to 0x100 in c100/dw0..dw2 only until its D beat plus 2 edges. After that, ie is assumed to still hold its old value (0) even though an unmodelled, error-free write to 0x100 may have changed IE_0. The assertion at lines 113-114 then requires o_intr_timer_expired=0. The contract text (contract.json:316) defines ie the same way, restricted to these two write kinds.

candidates.evidence_for: The ie model leaves out a legal write that changes IE_0. The register tool (lines 689-695) and the RTL PERMIT (rv_timer_reg_pkg.sv:150) both allow a 16-bit aligned write to a 1-bit register. D-013 says other sub-word cases are "not checked", so the checker may not assume they have no effect. As a result the checker treats IE_0 as 0 while the DUT correctly has IE_0=1, and the output IS_0&IE_0=1 is what D-005 requires.
candidates.evidence_against: The checker matches the contract's ie definition word for word (contract.json:316). The contract would need the same fix.

candidates.evidence_for: D-013 only lists full-word and byte-0 writes as checked cases. One could argue the bench should not issue other sub-word writes to INTR_ENABLE0.
candidates.evidence_against: No spec rule places that obligation on the environment. INT-TL-003 (lines 594-595) declares bad-size and bad-mask requests legal stimulus, and D-013 says only that such cases are "not checked". Adding an assumption that forbids them would hide behaviour without spec support.

candidates.evidence_for: None found. One would have to hold that a half-word write to INTR_ENABLE0 must not take effect.
candidates.evidence_against: The register tool error rule (opentitan_register_tool.md:689-693) applies only to writes smaller than the register, and the RTL follows it. The interrupt output equals IS_0&IE_0 as D-005 and CP-T1.8.6-04 require.

candidates.evidence_for: D-013 leaves the effect of 'other sub-word cases' unchecked, so the spec does not fix the IE value after a half-word write.
candidates.evidence_against: The register tool text is clear that a write whose size is not smaller than the register succeeds. The uncertainty only means the checker must not claim ie=0.

analyses.options: B (recommended), two choices. (1) In nnc_chk_intr.sv:68-70, let any error-free write (opcode 0/1, intg_flip=0, instr=0) to 0x100 with i_a_mask[0]=1 update ie from i_a_data[0] at its D beat. This matches the register-tool width rule and PERMIT 0001. (2) More conservatively, add an 'ie_unknown' flag that is set at the error-free D beat of any write to 0x100 that is not one of the modelled kinds. It disables CHK-004 until the next modelled write or reset. Update the contract's ie definition (contract.json:316) to match. Do not add an environment assumption that forbids half-word or other sub-word writes to 0x100: INT-TL-003 makes them legal stimulus. A side note, not the cause here: the checker's in-order queue (rp/wp FIFO) assumes in-order responses. TL-UL does not guarantee order (D-014), though this DUT allows only one outstanding request (tlul_adapter_reg.sv:231).

analyses.what_happens: Reset is asserted at edge 0 and released at edge 1. At edge 1, i_a_valid=0, as required. At edge 2 (rst_ni=1, rst_q=1) the host presents and the DUT accepts a PutFullData (opcode 0) with a_size=0, address 0x000, data 0x40000000, param 0, source 0 and mask 4'b1011 (11). 1011 is a non-contiguous mask, so bad_mask=1 and a_CHK_008 fails at edge 2. All other items hold at that edge: param=0, address<0x200, instr=0, source not outstanding, data!=1, not a CFG write. The DUT is not involved in the failure: the check is on stimulus only.
analyses.spec_says: opentitan_tlul_bus_specification.md:331-337 (TL-T3.1.3.4-02): "even though non-contiguous a_mask values like 0b1001 are permitted by the TL-UL spec, the TL-UL hosts within this project do not leverage non-contiguous masks. I.e., the TL-UL hosts will only assert a_mask values from the following restricted set for 32bit transfers: {'b0000, 'b0001, 'b0010, 'b0100, 'b1000, 'b0011, 'b0110, 'b1100, 'b0111, 'b1110, 'b1111}." rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:592-593 (INT-TL-003): "The test bench acts as the TL-UL host. It shall follow the host rules of the TL-UL bus specification". There is a tension with lines 594-595 ("Requests that the TL-UL specification lists as error cases (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address) are legal stimulus") and with the TL spec at line 365 ("Non-contiguous mask may lead to an error, depending on the device support"). D-013 (line 671): "Non-contiguous masks and other sub-word cases are not checked." The contract lists TL-T3.1.3.4-02 among the CHK-008 rules (contract.json:374).
analyses.rtl_does: Not relevant to the failure. For reference, tlul_err.sv:65 (`mask_chk = ~|(tl_i.a_mask & ~mask)`) would flag mask 1011 at a_size=0 as an error.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_tbhost.sv:52-54 defines bad_mask for 0101, 1001, 1010, 1011 and 1101. Lines 97-99 require !bad_mask whenever i_a_valid=1. This is an assertion on inputs, so in formal it can only hold if nnc_env.sv assumes the same obligation.

candidates.evidence_for: CHK-008 is a stimulus self-check, and every item it asserts must be assumed in the formal environment. nnc_env.sv (ENV-01..ENV-10, lines 108-162) has no assumption on a_mask. The obligation exists in the spec: TL-T3.1.3.4-02 (TL spec lines 331-337) says project hosts do not use non-contiguous masks, and INT-TL-003 (spec lines 592-593) binds the test bench to the TL-UL host rules. The contract cites TL-T3.1.3.4-02 for CHK-008.
candidates.evidence_against: INT-TL-003 (lines 594-595) also calls bad-mask requests legal stimulus, so a reviewer could argue non-contiguous masks are allowed error stimulus.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec says both that the host shall follow the TL-UL host rules, which exclude non-contiguous masks (TL 331-337), and that 'bad ... mask' error cases are legal stimulus (rv_timer spec 594-595). The TL spec (line 365) lists a non-contiguous mask as a possible error case. D-013 says only that non-contiguous masks are 'not checked'.
candidates.evidence_against: TL-T3.1.3.4-02 is specific about host behaviour (an explicit restricted mask set), and the contract has already taken it as a host obligation in CHK-008. 'Bad mask' in INT-TL-003 can be read as contiguous masks inconsistent with size or address.

candidates.evidence_for: If INT-TL-003 'bad ... mask' is read as including non-contiguous masks, the bad_mask item in the checker would be too strict.
candidates.evidence_against: The checker implements contract item (3) exactly, and that item is supported by TL-T3.1.3.4-02.

analyses.options: E (recommended): add to nnc_env.sv an assumption citing TL-T3.1.3.4-02 / INT-TL-003, for example `always @(*) if (i_a_valid) assume (!(i_a_mask inside {4'b0101,4'b1001,4'b1010,4'b1011,4'b1101}));`. Other CHK-008 items are also stricter in the checker than in nnc_env.sv and will likely produce the next counterexamples. (a) The checker forbids any write (any size or mask) to word 0x000 with i_a_data==0x00000001 (nnc_chk_tbhost.sv:102), while ENV-07 (nnc_env.sv:147-149) covers only effective full-word writes, with the condition data[0]&&!data[31]. (b) The checker's cfg_wr (lines 49-51) covers any write to the 0x10C/0x110/0x114 words, while ENV-08 covers only effective full-word writes. (c) The checker's active model updates at the error-free D beat (lines 67-71), while the env's f_active updates at acceptance (nnc_env.sv:98-103). The designer has to align each pair against D-002, D-009 and INT-TL-003. C: if the designer reads INT-TL-003 as allowing non-contiguous masks as error stimulus, record that in section 8. The bad_mask item would then have to be removed from CHK-008 and its contract text (B), and CHK-011/CHK-019 reviewed for how such requests are judged.
